difference_reason: DescrTab2 builds descriptive tables but its test-choice tree has no node for description itself. The UZH normality-check and z-standardisation statements are not adopted.

UZH leaf computes the pooled t-test and switches to Welch after a significant Levene test; DescrTab2 always gives Welch for 2 groups unless var_equal = TRUE. inferguidR uses Welch by default without a Levene gate.

DescrTab2 reaches the pooled t-test only through var_equal = TRUE (not drawn in the diagram); UZH computes the pooled t first. inferguidR offers it only when equal variances are justified in advance (status conditional).

Same test for two independent groups. UZH enters via 'distribution-free' and frames it as a median test; DescrTab2 enters via ordered factor or nonparametric = TRUE and reports a Hodges-Lehmann interval even on ordinal codes (Q05). inferguidR enters via ordinal outcome type or a rank estimand and reports the probability of superiority. Its p-value is computed under identical distributions; when spreads or shapes may differ it is not a valid test of a probability of superiority of 0.5, so inferguidR states this and lists Brunner-Munzel as the alternative (review 2026-10-03.2).

Both leaves compute the pooled-variance F test. UZH adds a Levene gate towards Welch/Brown-Forsythe; DescrTab2 ignores var_equal for 3+ groups (Q03). inferguidR keeps the pooled F only as a conditional outcome.
Welch ANOVA is named on the UZH page as a Levene-gated alternative and is not reachable in DescrTab2. It is inferguidR's default for more than two independent groups.
Same test. Both trees route by 'distribution-free' or ordered class rather than by estimand, and UZH frames it as a test of central tendency.
DescrTab2 handles a single grouping variable only.
Same test. DescrTab2 needs indices and drops incomplete pairs silently; inferguidR requires a confirmed ID (q.pairing_id) and asks about missing pairs (q.missingness).

UZH assistant routes interval-scaled paired data here (its page says 'at least ordinal'); DescrTab2 also routes ordered factors (integer codes) here. inferguidR uses it only for interval-level differences with a rank estimand.

For ordinal paired outcomes the UZH page offers the sign test, while DescrTab2 applies the Wilcoxon signed-rank test to integer codes. inferguidR follows the sign test because ordinal codes have no meaningful differences.

UZH assistant routes 'nominal' paired outcomes to the sign test. For a binary outcome the sign test on paired differences is the same binomial test on the discordant pairs as DescrTab2's exact McNemar test, so the two coincide; for 3+ unordered categories the sign test is undefined. inferguidR: binary -> exact conditional McNemar, nominal -> Stuart-Maxwell.
notes: rules: out.paired.mcnemar; out.paired.nominal. Refines uzh-tree.json condition_soundness 'incorrect' for the binary case.

difference_reason: Same design (3+ occasions, continuous outcome), different methods: UZH uses RM-ANOVA with Mauchly-gated GG/HF correction; DescrTab2 uses a random-intercept LMM labelled 'Mixed model ANOVA' (compound symmetry, Q15). inferguidR: complete data -> RM-ANOVA with routine GG correction; missing data -> LMM.
DescrTab2's random-intercept LMM corresponds to inferguidR's LMM outcome for repeated measures with missing data; inferguidR names the covariance structure explicitly.
Same test. DescrTab2 errors on incomplete blocks (Q12); UZH suggests Dunn-Bonferroni post hoc tests on mean ranks, which inferguidR does not adopt.

Both are Pearson chi-squared tests of independence. UZH applies Yates and sample-size thresholds; DescrTab2 uses no continuity correction. inferguidR uses no correction and pre-specifies the exact alternative from expected counts (q.small_expected).

UZH mentions Fisher's test for n < 20 or expected counts < 5; DescrTab2 uses Fisher when exact = TRUE and the table exceeds 2 x 2 or n > boschloo_max_n. inferguidR uses the Fisher-Freeman-Halton test when sparse expected counts are anticipated, never as an n-triggered switch away from Boschloo.
2 x 2 Fisher test: UZH via its n < 20 rule; DescrTab2 via exact = TRUE plus the n > 200 fallback (Q09). inferguidR uses it only when both margins were fixed by design.

UZH's contingency leaf is its only route for two independent binary groups and has no unconditional exact test. DescrTab2's Boschloo leaf (exact = TRUE, 2 x 2, nonmissing n <= 200) calls exact2x2::boschloo with tsmethod 'central'. inferguidR: Boschloo central for two independent binomial samples with fixed group sizes, no n cap, no Fisher substitution.
notes: rules: out.two_group.boschloo_central; exact2x2 1.7.0 tie-handling observation (2026-10-03) recorded in analysis-variants.json, open for 09A

difference_reason: The minlike two-sided variant, which the exact2x2 validation vignette checks, cannot be reached through descr() (Q16). inferguidR lists it as a separately labelled alternative variant.

DescrTab2 can pass alternative = 'less'/'greater' through additional_test_args (audit run R5), with orientation taken from level order (Q14). inferguidR offers one-sided only when pre-specified, with explicit event level and reference group.
UZH tests against a hypothesised probability; DescrTab2 fixes p0 = 0.5 and handles only 2 categories (G02, Q04). inferguidR requires a reference value fixed in advance.

UZH uses specified expected distributions (and also uses the test as a normality pre-test, not adopted); DescrTab2 tests only equal proportions. inferguidR requires fully specified expected proportions.
DescrTab2 has no association node. UZH routes here when no variable is designated as dependent; inferguidR routes by the symmetric-association aim and a linear estimand.
notes: rules: out.assoc.pearson; q.assoc_form; q.records_per_individual must be 'one' (review 2026-10-03.2)

difference_reason: UZH describes Spearman's coefficient as 'linear' (incorrect). inferguidR: monotonic association, for ordinal variables or a monotonic question.
UZH routes by presumed causal direction; inferguidR by the modelling aim (conditional mean of an outcome) without causal claims.
Stepwise selection described by UZH is not offered.
UZH assistant routes any nominal outcome here; inferguidR uses it for binary outcomes only (nominal -> multinomial, ordinal -> proportional odds).
notes: rules: out.model.logistic; out.model.multinomial; out.model.ordinal; q.records_per_individual must be 'one' (review 2026-10-03.2)

difference_reason: UZH illustrates factor analysis with PCA and the Kaiser criterion; inferguidR separates EFA (latent factors) from PCA and prefers parallel analysis.
PCA is UZH's worked example; inferguidR offers it as its own outcome for data reduction.
Ward hierarchical clustering follows the UZH example; mean imputation is not adopted.
UZH suggests downgrading mixed scale levels; inferguidR uses Gower dissimilarity instead.
Kept only as an alternative under normality and never as a pre-test.
Brown-Forsythe (median-centred Levene) is the robust between-group spread comparison recommended by inferguidR; UZH names Levene as a variant of the F test.
Not adopted as a route: a one-sample test against a known variance that requires normality. The UZH assistant reaches it via 'distribution-free' and frames it as a group comparison (incorrect).

DescrTab2's asymptotic McNemar uses stats::mcnemar.test with continuity correction and an unpaired interval (Q06). UZH has no McNemar node. inferguidR lists it as a labelled, not preferred alternative.
UZH has no Cochran's Q node. DescrTab2 errors on any missing response (Q12); inferguidR uses complete cases with reporting.
UZH has no one-sample t leaf. DescrTab2 tests against mu = 0 by default (Q04); inferguidR requires a reference value fixed in advance.

DescrTab2 applies the one-sample signed-rank test to ordinal integer codes against 0 (Q04). inferguidR rejects that for ordinal outcomes (sign test against a reference category instead) and lists the signed-rank test only as an alternative for continuous one-sample data.
Override-only in DescrTab2; inferguidR lists it as an alternative for a binary outcome across ordered groups.
Override-only in DescrTab2 (permutation p, no seed). inferguidR lists it as an alternative for ordered groups, with a recorded seed.

DescrTab2 'No test' outcomes map to explicit inferguidR outcomes: paired nominal with 3+ categories -> Stuart-Maxwell; exact one-sample with 3+ categories -> goodness of fit with specified proportions; a single supplied group (Q13) -> the one-sample route with a required reference value or needs_information.
Errors become typed advisor or engine statuses, never a silent p = NA.
inferguidR overrides are restricted to listed alternatives of the reached outcome; no user-supplied test functions.

UZH chooses the analysis family (description, dependence, interdependence); the DescrTab2 root selects one significance test per summarised variable. inferguidR asks for the aim/estimand with eight options.

Both separate related from independent samples. DescrTab2 makes this a user switch (paired = TRUE) per data type and requires indices; UZH asks it only within central tendency. inferguidR asks q.structure and then requires a confirmed ID.
